family_comparisons.name: Adaptive separator and treewidth bounds
family_comparisons.statement_boundary: Original-row public queries, arbitrary finite supports, helper/transcript-dependent separators, correlated correct set and arbitrary law; interaction graph differs from receiver side-information graph.
family_comparisons.contribution_claim: The displayed exact separator inequality, sharp deficit/helper coefficients, and derived finite treewidth bound in this model. Coefficient sharpness is universal, not established in the o(P) deficit/helper regime.
family_comparisons.novelty_status: Exact matching statement not identified in inspected sources; no exhaustive priority claim.

family_comparisons.name: Fixed two-coordinate Boolean packets and inverse-local recoding
family_comparisons.statement_boundary: Fixed one-bit functions of at most two stored coordinates. All-input independent row recoding retains exact bounds; the helper extension uses full-cube global bijections with declared inverse-row support, original-row side information, arbitrary input laws and charged helper entropy. Bounded-degree consequence also needs bounded inverse reuse and O(db) combined deficit.
family_comparisons.contribution_claim: Exact all-input bounds for arbitrary two-coordinate Boolean packets after independent bijective row recoding, with original XOR endpoints as direct corollaries; finite entropy bounds for helper-selected global bijections with declared inverse supports. Fixed degree, inverse width and reuse exclude fixed fractional savings for combined deficit/helper entropy o(P); the O(db) regime gives an explicit O(P/log d) error.
family_comparisons.novelty_status: New formal strengthening of this paper's restricted architecture theorem. Standard entropy and graph-cover ingredients are not claimed as newly discovered general principles. No exhaustive literature-priority certification; the earlier search record is retained with its original date.

family_comparisons.name: Countable affine motion and pointwise approximation
family_comparisons.statement_boundary: Actual normalized Lipschitz head limits with the imported cut condition; countable local branches; measured exceptions; fixed finite affine cover on the selected subsequence for approximation.
family_comparisons.contribution_claim: Quantitative exceptional-time bound and native correct-set/nonuniform/pointwise-error consequences.
family_comparisons.novelty_status: Klawe is relevant context but no implication/equivalence was established; no novelty claim for general affine nonexpansion.

family_comparisons.name: Fully paid native padding
family_comparisons.statement_boundary: One fixed native machine preserves arbitrary payloads with additive linear overhead and literal coarse-charge CutIneq; full M* conclusions apply to linear-time payload families. Data-free prefix; idle tapes disclosed.
family_comparisons.contribution_claim: Paid native implementation and scope consequence; analytic expander existence is credited to the literature.
family_comparisons.novelty_status: No prior statement with the same complete native/resource quantifiers identified in inspected sources; not an exhaustive compiler-literature search.

family_comparisons.name: Two-stage nonlinear helper barrier
family_comparisons.statement_boundary: Specified triangular bijection/causal-stage architecture, local wrappers, one charged helper choosing all architecture and orders; no free global middle operator.
family_comparisons.contribution_claim: All-split finite fiber cap and actual-helper-entropy charge under arbitrary input laws.
family_comparisons.novelty_status: Queries for triangular/two-stage transposition did not identify an equivalent theorem; generic entropy/fiber methods are established. Absence of a search hit is not a novelty proof.

family_comparisons.name: Native scan palettes and contracting regular recursion
family_comparisons.statement_boundary: Declared implemented palettes with bounded word lengths, or paid contracting stage clocks satisfying the precise affine regularity and exceptional-stage assumptions.
family_comparisons.contribution_claim: Native executors and their application to the geometric obstruction, including an explicit exceptional-work threshold.
family_comparisons.novelty_status: Prior one-tape bounds and standard recursive transpose methods have different machine/model hypotheses. No claim to exclude arbitrary coding recursion.
